tasks.short: Maintain timekeeping records, prepare payroll, resolve discrepancies and submit the approved pay run.

steps.what: Collect timekeeping records and employee changes from the {HCM}.
Request missing hours and corrections through the {EMAIL}.
Reconcile hours, rates and changes in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Enter approved changes and calculate the draft run in the {PAYROLL}.
Check pay variances and resolve exceptions in the {PAYROLL}.
Approve and submit the pay run through the {PAYROLL}.
File the submission receipt and supporting records in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure the {HCM}–{PAYROLL} connection and cutoff reminders, then add deterministic checks for missing hours, duplicate changes and unusual variances. A review queue in the {WORKFLOW} sends exceptions to the right person; submission requires payroll manager approval and automatically files the receipt in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local pay rules, inconsistent employee identifiers and separate approval records made the connections expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing import facilities and configurable rules cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector and validation development without changing payroll calculation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive corrections, disputed hours and national payroll rules need specialist handling. GDPR access controls and applicable national consultation rules still apply.
tasks.human_edge: Explain an unexpected pay change, resolve disputed hours and protect an employee from a technically valid but wrong payment.

ambition.what: Weekly missing-hours intervention before the payroll cutoff

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time copying records and more time resolving pay exceptions before cutoff. They can return incomplete inputs for correction within agreed rules; payroll approval rights stay with the payroll manager.

reach.task: Review recurring payroll preparation failures across departments.
reach.learn: Exception analysis, control ownership and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured payroll imports, cutoff checks and variance rules can automate preparation while retaining release approval.
The digest supplies no payroll-specific implementation case; the proposed savings require local validation.

assumptions: The assistant prepares payroll under a payroll specialist's supervision.
The {HCM} and {PAYROLL} support a configurable connector or controlled file import.
The {SPREADSHEET} reconciles gaps between systems rather than calculating statutory payroll.
Submission scope depends on the configured {PAYROLL}; bank payment release may be a separate treasury task.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Consent and access time includes permission setup and national consultation where applicable; waiting time may exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Which timekeeping and payroll interfaces are available?
Who approves time corrections, pay changes and final submission?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
How often do retroactive changes and disputed hours occur?
research_questions: Which existing configuration removes the most duplicate entry?
Which validation rules detect errors without creating excessive false alarms?
new_work: Maintain employee mappings, cutoff dates and validation thresholds.
Test rule changes against representative payroll cases.
Monitor import failures and retain approval evidence.

tasks.short: Collect receipts, deposit cash, prepare payments, disburse approved funds and reconcile account balances.

steps.what: Receive cash and count it against collection records.
Issue receipts and record collections in the {ERP}.
Deposit counted cash and obtain a deposit receipt.
Match supplier invoices to approvals and prepare payment proposals in the {ERP}.
Approve payment proposals and resolve exceptions in the {ERP}.
Authorize and release transfers through the {BANK}.
Pay approved petty-cash claims and obtain signed vouchers.
Reconcile statements, deposits and cash vouchers in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure collection records, invoice matching and payment proposals in the {ERP}, with an approved payment connection to the {BANK}. A deterministic reconciliation job matches references and amounts, leaving ambiguous transactions in a review queue; physical cash custody and payment authorization remain with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash evidence, bank statements and invoice approvals used different references. Finance controls also required a clear separation between preparation and release.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable payment batches, bank imports and small reconciliation programs can connect these records. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort; no model is needed for matching known references and amounts.
tasks.still_hard: Physical custody, cash shortages, changed bank details and disputed invoices require investigation. Bank access, segregation of duties and GDPR controls remain necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a suspicious request, explain a discrepancy and take responsibility for cash custody.

ambition.what: Daily investigation of aged unmatched cash transactions

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time rebuilding balances and more time investigating unexplained transactions. They can classify reconciliation exceptions within delegated limits; payment approval and bank mandates stay with authorized roles.

reach.task: Review petty-cash limits and the cost of handling physical collections.
reach.learn: Cash controls, exception ageing and process cost measurement.

evidence.claim: Payment proposals and reference-based bank reconciliation are established deterministic finance patterns.
Software can reduce recording work but does not remove physical cash handling or delegated payment responsibility.

assumptions: This company still has some physical collections and petty cash; many mid-size companies have little of either.
Supplier invoices already exist as structured records in the {ERP}.
Cash payments use previously approved claims within a delegated limit.
Automatic reconciliation posts only unique matches under approved rules.
The human classification reflects custody and authorization; much of the recording work is still automatable.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Access time includes bank mandates and national consultation where applicable; external waiting time can be longer.
unknowns: How much cash is handled, and could those collections move to existing electronic payment channels?
Which bank feeds and payment interfaces are available?
Who can change supplier bank details and who independently verifies those changes?
Which payment limits and dual-authorization rules apply?
research_questions: Can an existing electronic collection channel eliminate a physical cash route?
Which matching keys distinguish genuine matches from coincidental equal amounts?
new_work: Maintain payment limits and matching rules.
Periodically verify access rights and supplier-detail change controls.

tasks.short: Set clerical procedures, arrange staff coverage and adjust daily work when priorities change.

steps.what: Collect workload requests and deadlines through the {EMAIL}.
Discuss availability, skills and coverage problems with clerical staff.
Draft the clerical schedule in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Approve coverage trade-offs and the proposed schedule.
Update and circulate clerical procedures in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Current procedures, agreed changes and the approved procedure template.
loop.output: A revised procedure with a change list and links to each agreed change.
loop.check: Check every changed obligation against an agreed change; the assistant approves publication.
loop.stop: One draft per approved change batch, capped at 4,000 output tokens; unsupported changes return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Changes arrive as narrative instructions and need coherent rewriting across several procedure sections.

steps.what: Collate separate daily status emails into a progress list.
Discuss delays and agree daily work adjustments with clerical staff.

tasks.design: Configure a shared request queue in the {PROJECT}, with structured availability and a deterministic schedule generator that exposes coverage gaps for approval. Live task states replace the separate emailed progress list, while a bounded drafting loop updates procedures in the {DOCS} only after people agree the changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests, staffing constraints and progress reports were scattered across conversations and separate files. Coverage decisions also contain fairness and relationship considerations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared queues remove duplicate status collection. Small scheduling programs and bounded document drafting can now be built and adjusted with less development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Fair workload distribution, capability differences and urgent conflicts require discussion. GDPR and national employee consultation rules apply; introducing AI staff allocation or monitoring requires an EU AI Act classification assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate fair coverage, notice unspoken overload and decide when a service promise must change.

ambition.what: A daily coverage-gap decision before the first service deadline

tasks.altitude: The assistant uses a live workload view to negotiate coverage instead of collecting status reports. They can adjust work within agreed service priorities, while the manager retains decisions about staffing levels and material workload trade-offs.

reach.task: Plan capacity and manage dependencies across recurring office services.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, dependency mapping and explicit priority trade-offs.

evidence.claim: A government evaluation found drafting time savings but no demonstrated productivity improvement; scheduling took longer.
Structured constraints can generate a draft coverage schedule without a language model.
The EU AI Act's employment provisions can apply to AI systems used for staff allocation or monitoring.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent provisions cover relevant employee monitoring and personal-data arrangements.

assumptions: The assistant coordinates a small clerical team under an administrative services manager.
Scheduling uses explicit constraints rather than inferred employee performance scores.
Staff update task states directly in the {PROJECT}; this replaces the separate daily email digest.
The model drafts procedures only and does not allocate staff.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Consultation time is included where national rules require it; formal processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which decisions can the assistant make without manager approval?
Which coverage constraints and workload agreements apply?
Are task states already recorded in a shared system?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed visibility of staff work?
research_questions: Which minimum task states provide useful coverage information without unnecessary individual monitoring?
Can existing scheduling configuration express the constraints before custom code is built?
new_work: Maintain coverage constraints and request categories.
Review procedure drafts and check publication versions.
Review whether scheduling rules create recurring unfairness or unrealistic workloads.

tasks.short: Handle customer requests, check account information, enter orders and resolve service exceptions.

steps.what: Read customer emails and record the requested service.

loop.input: Customer email and a fixed service-request schema.
loop.output: Request type, customer reference, requested items and missing fields, with source excerpts.
loop.check: Validate the schema and compare extracted fields with source excerpts and permitted request types.
loop.stop: One extraction per message, capped at 2,000 output tokens; missing or ambiguous fields enter the manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Email requests describe items and intentions in varied free text; fixed forms remain the preferred intake route.

steps.what: Verify the customer and their account permissions in the {CRM}.
Look up account balances, order status and availability in the {ERP}.
Enter requested items and agreed terms as a draft order in the {ERP}.
Confirm the order or send account information through the {EMAIL}.
Discuss unusual requests, disputed information or unavailable items with the customer.

tasks.design: Offer a structured request form through the {WORKFLOW}, with a bounded extraction loop for remaining emails in the {EMAIL}. Deterministic connections retrieve authorized facts from the {CRM} and {ERP}, validate draft orders and populate response templates; the assistant approves disclosure and order confirmation, and handles exceptions by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer requests arrived in inconsistent language, while account facts and order entry lived in separate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake, permission-aware lookups and template responses handle the standard path. A small extraction loop can turn remaining free-text requests into reviewable fields.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, stale availability, unclear specifications and unusual commercial terms still cause exceptions. GDPR requires account information to reach only authorized recipients, and applicable EU AI Act transparency duties matter if a conversational AI channel is added.
tasks.human_edge: Understand an anxious or dissatisfied customer, negotiate a realistic alternative and recognize when a routine request hides a larger problem.

ambition.what: After-hours structured order intake for small customer accounts

tasks.altitude: The assistant checks ready-to-send facts and orders, then spends more time resolving exceptions. They can offer predefined alternatives within delegated terms; pricing exceptions and credit decisions remain with the responsible teams.

reach.task: Find recurring causes of incomplete requests and redesign customer intake.
reach.learn: Request taxonomy, completion-rate measurement and service process mapping.

evidence.claim: Structured forms, account lookups, order validation and template responses can handle standard service requests deterministically.
Free-text extraction needs validation and a fallback queue before its fields drive customer actions.
A government evaluation observed hallucinations and found no evidence of higher overall productivity.

assumptions: Routine requests are mainly emailed; unusual cases often move to a phone conversation.
Account inquiries skip draft-order entry; step shares represent the blended task across both request types.
Customer terms, item codes and relevant availability are available as structured records.
Draft orders do not trigger fulfillment or a binding confirmation before approval.
Account responses use templates populated from verified records rather than model-written factual answers.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Access time includes data permissions and national consultation where applicable; a customer-facing AI conversation is outside the initial scope.
unknowns: What proportion of requests concern orders, account information and exceptions?
Which identity checks are required for each information category?
Can the {ERP} create draft orders without triggering fulfillment?
Which alternatives and commercial terms can the assistant approve?
How current are stock, delivery and account data?
research_questions: Which request fields can become mandatory without causing customers to abandon intake?
What extraction error rate remains after source-linked review?
Which existing authenticated channel could remove repeated identity checks?
new_work: Review extracted requests and missing fields.
Maintain response templates, request categories and validation rules.
Monitor failed lookups, stale facts and duplicate order submissions.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving exceptions, coordinating service coverage and checking consequential actions. Decision rights grow within explicit correction and service limits; payroll release, payment authority and major staffing decisions remain delegated separately.
reach: Administrative services manager: improve recurring office controls and service capacity.
Project management specialist: coordinate workload, dependencies and coverage.
Management analyst: measure request failures and redesign intake.
skills_to_grow: Define validation rules and useful exception thresholds.
Check source records and approval evidence.
Map processes across systems and role boundaries.
Handle sensitive conversations and negotiate service trade-offs.
Understand GDPR, AI literacy and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: An office service coordinator who runs an early-warning review of pay-input gaps, unmatched cash, coverage shortages and unresolved customer requests, with authority to route corrections and propose changes backed by evidence.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
